7.text: the vaˊɪrg̣ɪt. The most important is the Polar Star, which is called in the
7.resolved: vaˊɪrg̣ɪt = v-a + U+02CA (stress) + ɪ (U+026A, small-cap) + r + g + U+0323 (combining dot below) + ɪ (U+026A) + t

8.text: Chukchee language Iluˊkälin eˊñer or Iluˊk-eˊñer (“motionless star”), or Äᵋlqeˊp-
8.resolved: Iluˊkälin = I-l-u + U+02CA (stress) + k + ä (a+U+0308) + l-i-n. eˊñer = e + U+02CA (stress) + ñ (n+U+0303) + e-r. Iluˊk-eˊñer = same eˊñer, prefixed Iluˊk (I-l-u + U+02CA + k) + hyphen. Äᵋlqeˊp- = Ä (A+U+0308) + ᵋ (U+1D4B, laryngeal superscript) + l-q-e + U+02CA (stress) + p + hyphen (word continues on line 9).
8.note: The raised mark between Ä and l read as ᵋ (U+1D4B) rather than ᵉ (U+1D49): per keying_spec.md §2.1/§2.6, ᵉ is licensed only immediately before i, and this sits before l — so under the disjoint-environment rule it cannot be ᵉ, and ᵋ is the only licensed candidate in this position. Shape at 4x (a small closed loop rather than a small 'e') is consistent with that reading.
